text:
sam_support: Heads-up — acme-prod reporting intermittent failures to their private service endpoint `svc.internal.acme` after a zone migration yesterday. 504s from our SDK and curl times out. customer pasted the failing curl output below.

acme_ops: curl -v https://svc.internal.acme/health
* Connected to svc.internal.acme (10.10.55.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number

sam_support: They said it "worked before the migration" and started flapping after they copied a private hosted zone from staging->prod and switched VPC associations.

maria_neteng: Can you paste `dig +short svc.internal.acme` from one of the failing hosts (the pod/node) and also run it repeatedly to show variance? Also confirm whether the VPC is associated to multiple private hosted zones with the same name across accounts.

acme_ops: Ran dig on a worker node, results:
```
$ dig +short svc.internal.acme @169.254.169.253
10.10.55.23
```
then after a retry:```
$ dig +short svc.internal.acme @169.254.169.253
10.200.77.9
```
So it flips between two IPs. One is an internal ALB in account A, the other looks like an internal NLB in account B (old staging).

jon_sre: That strongly smells like two private hosted zones with identical zone name attached to the same VPCs (Route53 allows private hosted zones with the same name in different accounts; resolution is ambiguous if both are associated). If the answer alternates it's probably because of resolver caching across nodes or multiple resolver endpoints returning different records.

maria_neteng: +1. Can you run these AWS checks from both accounts?
```
# account A (prod)
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "internal.acme" --query 'HostedZones[*].{Id:Id,Name:Name}'

# account B (staging)
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "internal.acme" --query 'HostedZones[*].{Id:Id,Name:Name}'
```
Also `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID --query 'VPCs'` to see VPC associations.

acme_ops: Ran those and confirmed: both accounts have a private hosted zone for `internal.acme`. Prod has Z-HOST-PROD associated to prod-VPCs, staging had Z-HOST-STG but we accidentally left staging Z-HOST-STG associated to the prod VPC during the migration window.

acme_ops: Output snippets:
```
# prod
{"VPCs": [{"VPCRegion":"us-east-1","VPCId":"vpc-prod-aaa"}]}
# staging
{"VPCs": [{"VPCRegion":"us-east-1","VPCId":"vpc-prod-aaa"}]}
```

sam_support: Ok that explains the flip. Route53 will answer records from any private hosted zone associated to the VPC that matches the query name, which can yield different records depending on which resolver/backend picks it up.

jon_sre: Two quick remediation options: 1) Disassociate the staging private hosted zone from the prod VPC (recommended), or 2) delete the staging zone if it's no longer needed. Also flush local resolver caches and reduce TTLs before migration to avoid long-lived cache surprises.

maria_neteng: Useful commands:
```
# disassociate the hosted zone from the VPC (run in staging acct)
aws route53 disassociate-vpc --hosted-zone-id Z-HOST-STG --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-prod-aaa

# verify
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z-HOST-STG --query 'VPCs'
```
Also check there are no Route53 Resolver rules that forward queries to an external resolver that might be returning stale answers.

acme_ops: We disassociated Z-HOST-STG from the prod VPC ~10m ago and reduced TTL to 30s before doing it. After disassociation, dig from a few nodes now consistently returns the prod ALB IP: `10.10.55.23`.

acme_ops: curl now:
```
$ curl -v https://svc.internal.acme/health
* Connected to svc.internal.acme (10.10.55.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* Server certificate: CN=svc.internal.acme
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

sam_support: Great — please monitor for a few TTL cycles and confirm. We'll note this as a config migration gotcha (private hosted zone leftover assoc). Thanks for quick turnaround. :white_check_mark:

jon_sre: Putting a short postmortem note in the ticket: cause = duplicate private hosted zone (same zone name) still associated to prod VPC after migration; impact = intermittent resolution and TLS/curl failures; remediation = disassociate old zone, verify VPC associations, TTL flush.

route53-bot: Ticket CREATED: #INC-2026-4827 linked to this thread.

acme_ops: Confirmed stable after 3mins, rolling back nothing. Appreciate the help — we'll add a pre-migration checklist item to drop prod assoc before cutover.

sam_support: Copy that. I'll close the support escalation once INC-2026-4827 is resolved.
